subject: Sunrise Labs: On-prem tail latency spikes and staged fallback plan
messages:
From: Anita Rao <anita@sunriselabs.io>
To: soojin_lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jeff Collins <jc@sunriselabs.io>, Sunrise Labs SRE <sre@sunriselabs.io>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden tail-latency & intermittent 503s on our on-prem cluster

Soojin —

We started seeing elevated tail latency around 08:30 this morning on our on-prem Redwood deployment (v1.4.2, GKE nodepool). P95 is fine but p99+/tail requests are taking 2–5s more than baseline and about 0.6% of requests are returning 503s for long-decoding prompts. This is impacting our user-facing batch inference and a couple of interactive endpoints.

Attached are a few traces and a sample of failed request headers. We pushed no code changes. We did change a cache TTL last week per your recommendations, but that was a smaller adjustment.

We need help urgently: telemetry to understand whether this is a model decode regression, KV-cache cold starts, or an autoscaler/backpressure problem. If you can propose a short mitigation plan (canary to lower-quant model, temporary rate-limiter, or config tweak), that would be appreciated. Our SRE team is standing by.

Thanks,
Anita Rao
Head of Platform, Sunrise Labs

Attachments: sunrise-traces-20270920.json
From: soojin_lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
To: Anita Rao <anita@sunriselabs.io>
Cc: dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Sunrise Labs SRE <sre@sunriselabs.io>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2027 09:36:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden tail-latency & intermittent 503s on our on-prem cluster

Anita —

Thanks for the traces and the heads-up. We’re treating this as a P2 escalation and I’ve looped in Dev (runtime) and our solutions lead. First steps:

- I’ll ask runtime to check decode kernel latencies and any recent scheduler/backpressure events.
- Please snapshot the pod logs for the affected time window and confirm if you still see 503s after 10:00.
- We’ll propose a staged fallback (canary to a quantized-compatible variant and a temporary rate cap on long requests) while we triage.

We’ll follow up within 2 hours with a proposed mitigation. If you prefer, we can take this to a short bridge.

— Soojin Lee
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
From: dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: soojin_lee <soojin@redwood.ai>, grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2027 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Sudden tail-latency & intermittent 503s on our on-prem cluster

Quick findings after a first-pass from runtime:

- The traces show long tail time is dominated by repeated decode stalls around KV-cache misses for long-prefix prompts ( >800 tokens). There are also short-lived GC-like stalls in the node metrics coincident with those traces.
- Autoscaler looks healthy but we see repeated small backoffs from the internal batching queue when multiple long requests arrive simultaneously — appears to be head-of-line blocking in continuous batching.
- There is a config drift: prefix_cache.max_entries on the customer operator is set to 16k; our recommended prod setting for their workload is 64k. That would explain higher miss rates.

Immediate remedial actions I recommend (playbook steps attached):
1) Increase prefix_cache.max_entries to 64k and stagger restart across pods (apply to one AZ at a time).
2) Enable per-request decode-timeout for requests > 1k tokens and return partials instead of 503s as a temporary measure.
3) Canary a lower-precision (int8) model variant on 10% of traffic for long prompts to reduce decode latency; route by header or HubSpot flag.
4) Short-term: throttle large-batch concurrent window to avoid head-of-line blocking; increase batching worker threads by +2 on the affected nodepool.

I attached flame graphs and the quick playbook: playbook-kv-cache-adjustments.pdf, flamegraph-decode-20270921.svg.

— Dev Patel
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachments: playbook-kv-cache-adjustments.pdf; flamegraph-decode-20270921.svg

Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden tail-latency & intermittent 503s on our on-prem cluster

Anita —

We can execute Dev’s plan. High-level ask for your team: please confirm a maintenance window today (we recommend 13:00–14:00 PT) to increment prefix cache and run the rolling restart. During the window we’ll also deploy the 10% int8 canary and enable decode-timeout behavior.

If that window works we’ll:
- Run a read-only roll first (apply config to one pod, validate traces),
- Then a staged restart across AZs,
- Monitor p99, error rate, and pod restarts.

If you’d prefer not to restart today we can schedule tomorrow morning; the quicker we act the less customer impact.

— Grace O’Connor
Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2027 08:46:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Sudden tail-latency & intermittent 503s on our on-prem cluster — playbook and rollback plan

Following up with a concise playbook and timeline for the maintenance window (also added to the Confluence doc):

T-minus 0: Pre-checks (verify node metrics, confirm no config drift in autoscaler) — 15m
T+15: Apply prefix_cache.max_entries=64k to pod-0 in zone-a & enable per-request decode-timeout — 10m validate
T+30: Canary int8 model variant on 10% traffic (route by header) — 15m validate
T+60: Rolling restart across remaining pods (stagger 5m per pod) — 30–45m
T+120: Full validation period: run synthetic long prompt suite against canary and baseline; monitor p99/p999 and 503 rate — 60m
Rollback criteria: if p999 increases by >10% or 503 rate increases above 1% or CPU/GPU OOMs are seen.

I’ve uploaded a PDF with the exact commands and k8s patch snippets (playbook-kv-cache-adjustments.pdf) to the Confluence link.

— Markus Klein
Lead Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: soojin_lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
To: Anita Rao <anita@sunriselabs.io>, Jeff Collins <jc@sunriselabs.io>
Cc: dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2027 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Sunrise Labs — Proposed remediation schedule and next steps

Anita / Jeff —

Thanks for aligning on the window. Summary of agreed plan and ask:

1) Maintenance window: Wed 22 Sep 2027, 13:00–15:00 PT (we will proceed unless you flag a hard no before 11:00 PT).
2) Actions: increase prefix_cache.max_entries -> 64k (staggered), enable decode-timeout for >1k token requests, canary int8 variant at 10% traffic, temporary throttle on large concurrent batch size.
3) Owners: Redwood runtime (Dev/Markus) will execute config changes and canary; Sunrise SRE will monitor node health and alert on OOMs.
4) Rollback: immediate rollback if p999 worsens by >10% or 503s exceed 1% for a sustained 10m window.

We’ve prep’d the playbook and will provide a dedicated bridge channel during the operation. Please confirm by 11:00 PT today or we’ll assume consent to proceed.

Best,
— Soojin Lee
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
